archetype.name: Play-In Team (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A roster whose defense and frontcourt keep it near .500. The offense has ranked in the bottom third for years, which keeps it in the East's middle tier rather than among the contenders.

report.headline: New shot diet, same broken offense, and now Banchero is out
report.take:
Three games in, Orlando looks like the team it has been for five years: a competent defense attached to an offense that can't score. The Magic sit 26th in offensive rating at 106 and 14th in defensive rating at 112.5, which adds up to a -6.5 Net Rtg and 20th on the site. History says this isn't new. The offense ranked 26th, 27th, 22nd and 19th across the last four seasons, while the defense carried them to 47-35 and 45-37 finishes. The 1-2 start fits the margin exactly; W vs Pt Diff is 0, so there is no luck to unwind in either direction.

The real change is the shot profile. Orlando's 3PA Rate is 47.1, third in the league, well above the league's 41.9 and far above last season's 38.6. The shots aren't falling at 32.2% from three, and the move outside has cost them on the glass. Their ORB % of 20.8 ranks 28th, seven points below the league average, after three straight seasons around 25. Taking more threes without making them, and without second chances, is a worse version of the old problem. The guards are where it hurts most. Jalen Suggs is at a 40.3 TS % and Desmond Bane at 49.3, and the backcourt grades a D. Franz Wagner is using 31.7% of possessions on the floor at a 49.5 TS %.

The scoring that has worked has come from inside. Wendell Carter Jr. is shooting a 86.7 TS % and Paolo Banchero a 77, which is why the frontcourt grades A-. That grade won't survive. Carter's efficiency is a three-game number, and Banchero is listed Out after two games. Colin Castleton ranking first on the center tab off 4 minutes is pure noise. Anthony Black's one game (18 points, 5 threes, a 75.8 TS %) is the brightest spot in the backcourt, and it is also one game.

The defense is the part to trust. Opponents' eFG % of 50.7 ranks 10th, and their 64.2% at the rim ranks 12th, even though Orlando lets them get there often (Opp Rim Rate 33.9, 23rd). Defending without forcing turnovers (Opp TOV % 12.3, 22nd) and without securing the defensive glass (DRB % 69.8, 22nd) caps how good it can be. With Banchero out, the offense has to find answers from guards who haven't supplied any yet.

strengths.title: Frontcourt efficiency inside the arc
strengths.body: Carter and Banchero have been the offense's only reliable source of points, both scoring at elite efficiency with moderate usage. The frontcourt's listed players lead the roster groups in points despite the fewest minutes. Carter's rate will fall back to earth. With Banchero out, the group's grade is likely to slide from A-.

strengths.title: Shot defense still holds up
strengths.body: Opponents shoot below the league in eFG % and at the rim, which matches a franchise that posted top-two defenses two and three seasons ago. The weak spots are that it concedes rim attempts and doesn't force turnovers. The base is real and should keep the Magic competitive most nights.

concerns.title: More threes, fewer makes, no rebounds
concerns.body: Orlando has jumped to third in 3PA Rate while shooting below the league from deep. Its offensive rebounding has collapsed to 28th, well under the roughly 25% it posted the last three seasons. If the shooting doesn't come around, this volume is a step backward for an offense that was already bottom-third.

concerns.title: Backcourt can't create efficiently
concerns.body: Suggs and Bane have taken the bulk of the guard minutes at well below average efficiency. Both carry negative BPMs, and Suggs is day-to-day. Opposing shooting guards have also taken a far larger share of the points against Orlando than the league norm. The guards are losing at both ends so far.

concerns.title: Banchero out, usage falls on Wagner
concerns.body: Losing the most efficient high-usage scorer pushes even more on Wagner, who is already using 31.7% of possessions at a sub-50 TS %. Until Banchero returns, the offensive rating has little room to climb.

trend.note: The Magic opened with a 125-132 home loss to Atlanta and a 93-115 home loss to Minnesota, then won 111-102 at New York. Three games swinging between shootout, blowout and grind don't establish a direction yet.

weekAhead.headline: Two at Toronto's elite defense, then Boston and Washington home
weekAhead.body:
The week starts with back-to-back road games in Toronto. The Raptors are eighth on the site, third in defensive rating at 98.8, and first in forcing turnovers. That is a bad pairing for an Orlando offense that already turns it over at a 21st-ranked rate. Toronto's own offense is shooting 26.2% from three and sits 29th in eFG %. These should be low-scoring games decided by whether Orlando's defense can keep a poor shooting team cold while protecting the ball.

The homestand is friendlier. Boston ranks 21st in defensive rating, 27th in DRB %, and is near the bottom in rebounds per game. That gives Orlando's missing offensive glass a chance to show up, although Boston's 39.5% three-point shooting tests the perimeter defense. Washington gets to the line more than anyone and defends the three well (Opp 3P % 28.8, fourth). It has also given up heavy scoring to small forwards, an opening for Wagner and Da Silva. A split of the week would be a reasonable result. Two wins in Toronto would be a real signal.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security against Toronto's pressure
keyMatchups.body: Toronto forces turnovers at the league's best rate, while Orlando's TOV % is worse than the league. With Banchero out, more ball-handling falls on guards who have struggled. Coughing it up twice on the road could decide both games.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Boston
keyMatchups.body: Boston's 67.5 DRB % ranks 27th and it has allowed 26 points a game to centers. This is the spot for Carter to keep producing and for Orlando to recover some of its missing offensive rebounds.

keyMatchups.title: Wings against Washington, fouls the other way
keyMatchups.body: Washington has allowed 31.33 points a game to small forwards, 27th in the league, which suits Wagner and Da Silva. But the Wizards' league-best FT Rate will test a defense that otherwise keeps opponents' shooting down.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Orlando keeps launching threes at a 47% rate without Banchero, or leans on Carter and attacks the paint.

restOfSeason.body:
The 27-win pace is three games of noise layered on a missing star. This franchise has won 41 to 47 games three straight years on the strength of its defense. The defense looks intact, and the shooting should drift up from 32.2% toward the league. The bigger questions are structural. Can an offense built around a jump in three-point volume work when the team has never shot it well? How long is Banchero out? Carter's and Black's hot starts will cool, so the guards have to become at least average for the offense to climb out of the bottom five.

Expect a team hovering around .500 with a defensive rating near the league average and an offense still bottom-third, landing in the play-in range rather than above it. If Banchero returns soon and the backcourt finds efficiency, a repeat of last season's 45-37 is reachable. If the three-point bet keeps missing and the glass stays this weak, the low end comes into play.
swingFactors: Whether the three-point volume starts converting
Backcourt efficiency from Suggs and Bane

confidence.note: Three games, a key scorer out, and per-player rates on tiny minutes.
